newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling firm on low dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling firm on low dollar demand.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling maintained its steady creep higher on Friday as demand for dollars remained extremely low, forex dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 54.63 against the dollar compared to 54.65 on Thursday.
Against the British pound it was posted at a mean rate of 89.78 from 89.89.
"Demand for the dollar is still very low and unless this situation changes, we expect the shilling to maintain its bullish tone," a commercial bank dealer said.
For the last two months dollar demand has been low, while inflows from traditional coffee and tea sales have been supplemented by an unanticipated increase of from foreign investors.
Dealers said the central bank, which checked the shilling's appreciation in late February and early March, had kept off the market.
"It looks like they are letting rates adjust themselves," another dealer said.
The money market was liquid with overnight rates quoted between 5-10 percent compared to Thursday's 8-12 percent.
